title: PetroNusa Q4 2025 gasoline grade ladder: state take vs commercial value
prompt:
You are a consultant at Aurelian & Co. on the PetroNusa engagement (downstream fuel retail, Republic of Sariwon).

The CFO's pricing review has asked a simple question that nobody in the client team can answer consistently: on the Q4 2025 posted pump prices, how much of each gasoline grade's price is taken by the state, and how much of the headline price ladder between grades is real commercial value? Management keeps quoting the SRP 2,600 per litre gap between RON 95 and RON 90 as the premium the network earns for upgrading a customer, and Commercial Finance disputes it.

Using the files in the folder, and stating every figure on the basis Commercial Finance uses for competitive and cross-grade benchmarking (their standing guidance is in the folder — say clearly which basis each figure is on), produce for Q4 2025:

1. For RON 90, RON 92 and RON 95: the total per-litre amount taken by the state on each grade (all taxes, duties and levies that apply to that grade), and the per-litre value remaining to the business on the Commercial Finance basis.
2. The state take on RON 95 expressed as a percentage of its posted pump price.
3. The RON 95-over-RON 90 price ladder: the gap on the Commercial Finance basis, in SRP per litre, and that gap expressed as a percentage of the headline posted-price gap — i.e. how much of management's quoted premium actually survives.
4. A short note on where the folder's own commentary about these taxes is imprecise or misleading.

Save your deliverable as `grade_ladder_state_take.md` — a short memo with the per-grade table, the derivation of each figure, the basis used, and your caveats.

checks.description: Total per-litre state take on RON 90 at the Q4-2025 posted price of 12,300: VAT 12,300 - 12,300/1.11 = 1,218.92, plus excise 340, plus Energy Price Stabilisation Fund 25 (subsidised grades only) = 1,583.92 SRP/l.

refs.name: espf
refs.quote: An Energy Price Stabilisation Fund contribution of SRP 25 per litre applies to subsidised grades only

checks.report_ask: Report the total per-litre amount taken by the state on RON 90 at its Q4 2025 posted pump price, in SRP per litre.

decoy.description: Naive path: VAT (correctly de-grossed) plus excise only, omitting the stabilisation-fund contribution that applies to subsidised grades.

checks.description: RON 92 value on the Commercial Finance basis: 13,600 / 1.11 - 900 = 11,352.25 SRP/l.

refs.name: basis
refs.file: Commercial Finance note - premium netback basis.docx
refs.quote: pump value less VAT, less excise duty

checks.report_ask: Report the per-litre value remaining to the business on RON 92 at its Q4 2025 posted pump price, on the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, in SRP per litre.

decoy.description: Naive path: applying the premium (RON 95) excise rate of 1,250 to RON 92 as well.

checks.description: RON 95 value on the Commercial Finance basis at Q4-2025 posted price: 14,900 / 1.11 - 1,250 = 12,173.42 SRP/l.
checks.report_ask: Report the per-litre value remaining to the business on RON 95 at its Q4 2025 posted pump price, on the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, in SRP per litre.

decoy.description: Naive path: pump price less excise, leaving embedded VAT in the figure.

checks.description: State take on RON 95 as a share of its Q4-2025 posted price: (14,900 - 14,900/1.11 + 1,250) / 14,900 = 18.30%.
checks.report_ask: Report the total state take on RON 95 as a percentage of its Q4 2025 posted pump price.

decoy.description: Naive path: 11% of the VAT-inclusive pump price plus excise, over pump price.

checks.report_ask: Report the RON 95 over RON 90 price gap for Q4 2025 on the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, in SRP per litre.

decoy.description: Naive path: management's headline posted-price gap, 14,900 - 12,300.

checks.description: Share of the headline RON 95 over RON 90 posted-price gap surviving on the Commercial Finance basis: 1,432.34 / 2,600 = 55.09%.
checks.report_ask: Report the Q4 2025 RON 95 over RON 90 gap on the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis as a percentage of the headline posted-price gap between the two grades.

decoy.description: Naive path: restating the gap for VAT only and ignoring that excise differs sharply by grade, giving 1/1.11 = 90.09%.

difficulty_rationale: Three traps stack. (a) Pump prices are VAT-INCLUSIVE, so VAT per litre is price x 0.11/1.11, not price x 0.11. (b) Excise is grade-specific (RON 90: 340, RON 92: 900, RON 95: 1,250) and the SRP 25/l Energy Price Stabilisation Fund contribution applies ONLY to subsidised grades, i.e. to RON 90 and not to RON 92/95 — most analysts either apply the premium excise across grades or drop the levy entirely. (c) Because excise rises steeply up the ladder, management's SRP 2,600 pump gap between RON 95 and RON 90 collapses to SRP 1,432 on the Commercial Finance basis, i.e. only ~55% survives; the naive VAT-only restatement gives ~90%.

--- Output format requirement (machine-graded) ---
Alongside your deliverable(s), write a `report.json` in your output directory with
exactly these top-level keys, each set to the plain number (or value) your analysis
supports — no prose, no nesting, no units in the value:

- `result_01` — Report the total per-litre amount taken by the state on RON 90 at its Q4 2025 posted pump price, in SRP per litre. (unit: SRP per litre)
- `result_02` — Report the per-litre value remaining to the business on RON 92 at its Q4 2025 posted pump price, on the Commercial Finance benchmarking basis, in SRP per litre. (unit: SRP per litre)

- `result_04` — Report the total state take on RON 95 as a percentage of its Q4 2025 posted pump price. (unit: pct)

Your work is graded programmatically from `report.json` and the deliverable files.
A key that is missing, renamed, wrapped in a container, or given as prose scores zero.
